mainTopic: Why would we ever think that an ערוה like אחות אשה could go to יבום? The גמרא drops one explanation (the rule of דבר שיצא מן הכלל) and offers another (a מה מצינו from אשת אח).
overview: Before this section, the גמרא asked why the תורה needed a special word to stop אחות אשה from going to יבום. Here it first finishes the example of the מצורע's אשם, which needs a פסוק to bring it back to the normal rules of the מזבח. It then rejects that rule as the reason for the mistaken thought, because an exception left alone stays narrow: only אשת אח would be permitted. Instead it suggests a מה מצינו from אשת אח. It challenges this, since אחות אשה carries two איסורים. It answers that we might have reasoned: once the תורה permitted her, she stays permitted. To show that this reasoning exists, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about a מצורע who had a קרי on his eighth day, which fell on ערב פסח. The ברייתא lets him enter, and רבי יוחנן adds that the ban on a טבול יום entering is only rabbinic. עולא explains the ruling: since he was permitted despite his צרעת, he is permitted despite his קרי. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to ask whether עולא's case really matches the case of יבום, a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse returns the מצורע's guilt-offering to its usual rules
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'כי כחטאת האשם הוא' teaches that the אשם of a מצורע still needs its blood and fats put on the מזבח, just like a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'For as the sin-offering, so is the guilt-offering.' Just as a sin-offering needs its blood and fats placed on the altar, the guilt-offering does too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its example of the rule about something taken out of a category and then brought back. A פסוק is needed to put the מצורע's אשם back under the normal laws of the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אשם of a מצורע was pulled out of the usual אשם rules to teach something new: its blood goes on the person's thumb and toe. Without a פסוק, we might think it also loses the normal requirement of blood and fats on the מזבח. 'כי כחטאת האשם הוא' brings it back for that requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches; introduces a פסוק as a source
Guilt-offering; here, the one brought by a מצורע
Placing the blood on the altar
The fats and parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: The verse states:
"For as the sin-offering, so is the guilt-offering."
Just as a sin-offering requires
placing of the blood and the sacrificial parts on the altar,
so too the guilt-offering requires
placing of the blood and the sacrificial parts on the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: כִּי כַּחַטָּאת הָאָשָׁם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the example of the אשם מצורע begun before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That an item taken out of a category to teach something new needs an explicit פסוק to return to that category.

steps.title: That rule does not explain the mistaken thought
steps.stepSummary: Without the פסוק we would have kept the אשם out only for its new law. In the same way, only אשת אח would be permitted, and all other עריות would stay forbidden. So this rule cannot be why we might think אחות אשה goes to יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the verse had not brought it back, I would have said: it is taken out only for what it was taken out for, and not for anything else. Here too: a brother's wife, who was permitted, is permitted. Other forbidden women are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the rule about returning something to its category does not create a reason to think other עריות are permitted for יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a פסוק, the rule only limits things: the exception stays narrow. Applied to יבום, the exception is אשת אח alone, and every other ערוה stays forbidden. So this rule gives no reason to think אחות אשה could go to יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: Brought it back (to the general category)
Went out, was taken out of the category
A brother's wife, normally forbidden but permitted for יבום

phrases.english: And had the verse not brought it back,
I would have said:
for the matter it was taken out for, it is taken out,
and for the matter it was not taken out for, it is not taken out.
Here too, I would have said:
a brother's wife, who was permitted, is permitted,
phrases.notes: Some versions add the letter in square brackets; either way the word means 'was permitted.'

phrases.english: but the other forbidden relations are not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא אַהְדְּרֵיהּ קְרָא הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the אשם example to show the rule cannot be the source of the mistaken idea.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the rule of דבר שיצא מן הכלל to explain why we might think עריות go to יבום.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Without a פסוק, that rule only keeps the exception narrow. It would permit אשת אח and nothing more.
steps.whatToRemember: An exception left without a פסוק stays narrow: only אשת אח is permitted, not other עריות.

steps.title: A new reason for the mistaken thought: compare to a brother's wife
steps.stepSummary: The real reason we might have thought it is a מה מצינו: just as אשת אח, normally forbidden, goes to יבום, so should אחות אשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you might have thought: learn it through 'what do we find' from a brother's wife. Just as a brother's wife does יבום, so should a wife's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different reason someone might think אחות אשה could go to יבום: a comparison to אשת אח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אשת אח is normally an ערוה, yet the תורה permits her for יבום. A מה מצינו copies that result to another ערוה, אחות אשה. This is the mistaken thought the special word in the פסוק comes to block.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier idea and offers a new one
'What do we find': learning one case from a similar case

phrases.english: Rather, it would have entered your mind to say:
Let it be learned through "what do we find" from a brother's wife.
Just as a brother's wife goes into יבום,
so too a wife's sister should go into יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: תֵּיתֵי בְּמָה מָצִינוּ מֵאֵשֶׁת אָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation rejected in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new reason for the mistaken thought.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מה מצינו from אשת אח would allow אחות אשה to go to יבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: This possible mistake is why the תורה needed a special word excluding אחות אשה.

steps.title: Is the comparison fair? One prohibition versus two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the מה מצינו. אשת אח has one איסור, but a widow who is also אחות אשה has two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it comparable? There, there is one prohibition. Here, there are two prohibitions!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the comparison from step 3 as too weak for anyone to have suggested it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normal יבום overrides only one איסור, אשת אח. When the widow is also the sister of the יבם's own wife, there is a second איסור, אחות אשה. Overriding one איסור does not show you can override two.

phrases.english: Is it comparable?
There, there is one prohibition;
here, there are two prohibitions!
phrases.notes: The two are אשת אח and אחות אשה, both on the same woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי? הָתָם חַד אִיסּוּרָא הָכָא תְּרֵי אִיסּוּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the מה מצינו offered in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The מה מצינו comparing אחות אשה to אשת אח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A case with one איסור cannot teach a case with two, so no one would make this comparison.

steps.title: Once permitted, she stays permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might still have reasoned: since the תורה permitted the brother's wife for יבום, she stays permitted even with a second איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since she was permitted, she is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the comparison. It shows why someone could still have thought the second איסור does not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the מצוה of יבום fully removes her forbidden status. If that is true, it would not matter how many איסורים she has. Because this mistake was possible, the תורה needed to teach clearly that אחות אשה does not go to יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: Lest you say; introduces a mistaken thought the source comes to block

phrases.english: Lest you say:
since she was permitted, she is permitted.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the mistaken thought was still reasonable.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since יבום permits אשת אח, it removes every איסור she has, even a second one.
steps.terutzMaskana: That mistake was possible, so a source was needed to exclude אחות אשה from יבום.
steps.whatToRemember: The mistaken thought is: since יבום permitted her, she is fully permitted, even with a second איסור like אחות אשה. The תורה had to block this.

steps.title: Looking for a source and bringing the case of the מצורע on ערב פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we find the rule 'since it was permitted, it stays permitted,' and brings a ברייתא about a מצורע who became a טבול יום on ערב פסח and is still allowed in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we see that once something is permitted, it stays permitted? From a ברייתא: a מצורע's eighth day fell on ערב פסח. That day he had a קרי and immersed. The חכמים said: even though any other טבול יום may not enter, this one may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the reasoning from Step 5 and begins to answer with a ברייתא. This sets up the proof, which comes into focus with עולא in Step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 relied on the idea that a permission stays in force even when a second איסור is added. Here the גמרא looks for this idea in another area of הלכה. In the ברייתא's case, a person who would normally be kept out because he is a טבול יום is still let in.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it was permitted, it stays permitted
A person with the skin affliction צרעת
The eighth day, when the מצורע brings his final offerings
A seminal emission, which makes a person טמא
Someone who immersed today but must wait for nightfall to become fully טהור

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a ברייתא about יבום at all. The גמרא is borrowing a rule from the laws of טומאה to support the reasoning it used about יבום.

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that we say: since it was permitted, it stays permitted?
As it is taught in a ברייתא:
A מצורע whose eighth day fell
on the eve of פסח,
and he had a seminal emission on that day, and immersed,
the Sages said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין טְבוּל יוֹם אַחֵר נִכְנָס,
phrases.english: even though any other טבול יום may not enter,
this one may enter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָא תֵּימְרָא דְּאָמְרִינַן הוֹאִיל וְאִישְׁתְּרִי אִישְׁתְּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Seeks a source for the reasoning used in Step 5.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the מצורע who became a טבול יום on ערב פסח

steps.title: The ברייתא gives its reason: a stronger מצוה pushes aside a weaker one
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that the מצוה of the קרבן פסח, which carries כרת, should push aside the מצוה of keeping a טבול יום out, which does not carry כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is better that a מצות עשה with כרת should come and push aside a מצות עשה without כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why this מצורע is allowed in. Bringing the קרבן פסח is so important that it wins over the rule keeping a טבול יום out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not bringing the קרבן פסח is punished with כרת. The rule against a טבול יום entering is only a מצות עשה with no כרת. So the stronger מצוה overrides the weaker one.

keyTerms.meaning: Being cut off, a severe heavenly punishment

phrases.aramaic: מוּטָב שֶׁיָּבֹא עֲשֵׂה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ כָּרֵת
phrases.english: It is better that a positive מצוה that has כרת should come
phrases.notes: That is the קרבן פסח: someone who skips it gets כרת.

phrases.english: and push aside a positive מצוה that has no כרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּטָב שֶׁיָּבֹא עֲשֵׂה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ כָּרֵת וְיִדְחֶה עֲשֵׂה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא's own reason for the ruling in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מצות עשה with כרת (קרבן פסח) overrides a מצות עשה without כרת (keeping a טבול יום out).

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: by תורה law there is not even a מצות עשה here
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that by תורה law a טבול יום may enter this area. The ban is a later rabbinic rule, hinted at in a פסוק about the 'new courtyard.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: by תורה law there is not even a מצות עשה here, as it says: 'And יהושפט stood in the congregation of יהודה before the new courtyard.' What is 'the new courtyard'? It is where they made new rules and said: a טבול יום may not enter the מחנה לויה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds that the ban on a טבול יום entering this area is not from the תורה at all. The חכמים made it, and the פסוק's 'new courtyard' hints at this new rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spoke as if a real מצות עשה was being pushed aside. רבי יוחנן says the תורה itself never forbade it. So the מצורע's entry only overrides a rabbinic rule.

keyTerms.meaning: By תורה law, from the תורה itself
The camp of the לויים, the area of the הר הבית

phrases.english: And רבי יוחנן said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה אֲפִילּוּ עֲשֵׂה לֵית בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: By תורה law, there is not even a positive מצוה involved,
phrases.notes: He means the תורה itself never forbade a טבול יום to enter here; the ban came later from the חכמים.

phrases.english: as it is said:
'And יהושפט stood in the congregation of יהודה
before the new courtyard.'
What is 'the new courtyard'?
He said:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the name רבי יוחנן here and some don't; either way it is still his explanation.

phrases.english: That they made new rulings there, and said:

phrases.aramaic: טְבוּל יוֹם לֹא יִכָּנֵס לְמַחֲנֵה לְוִיָּה.
phrases.english: a טבול יום may not enter the camp of the Levites.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה אֲפִילּוּ עֲשֵׂה לֵית בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the ברייתא's reasoning by saying the ban being overridden is only rabbinic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By תורה law a טבול יום may enter the מחנה לויה; the ban is a rabbinic rule, hinted at by 'the new courtyard.'

steps.title: עולא's reason: permitted for his צרעת, so permitted for his קרי
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that since the תורה let the מצורע in despite his צרעת, he is also let in despite his קרי. This is the proof for 'once permitted, it stays permitted.'
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: What is the reason? Since he was permitted despite his צרעת, he is permitted despite his קרי.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the heart of the proof. עולא says the מצורע may enter because the permission he already had despite his צרעת carries over to his new טומאה of קרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצורע already had a permission to enter even though he was not fully טהור from his צרעת. When a second problem, his קרי, is added, the permission still holds. This matches the reasoning in Step 5: the brother's wife stays permitted even when a second איסור is added.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the actual source the גמרא was looking for in Step 6. If it holds, it supports the idea that the brother's wife stays permitted for יבום even when she is also אחות אשה.

phrases.english: And עולא said: What is the reason?
Since he was permitted despite his צרעת,
phrases.notes: The תורה let him in to finish his purification while he still had some טומאה left from his צרעת.

phrases.english: he is permitted despite his seminal emission.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר עוּלָּא: מַה טַּעַם? הוֹאִיל וְהוּתַּר לְצָרַעְתּוֹ הוּתַּר לְקִרְויוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the reasoning that turns the ברייתא of Step 6 into a proof for Step 5's logic.
steps.raayaObject: The principle הואיל ואישתרי אישתרי used in Step 5
steps.raayaSupportSource: עולא's explanation of the ברייתא: הואיל והותר לצרעתו הותר לקרויו

steps.title: Is עולא's case really comparable?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to push back on the proof by asking whether עולא's case really matches the case of יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really comparable to עולא's case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to question the proof it just brought. This line sets up the next move, where it will explain how the two cases differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works only if the מצורע's case and the יבום case are built the same way. The גמרא is now challenging that match. The explanation of the difference comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Is it comparable to the case of עולא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to reject the proof from עולא brought in Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The use of עולא's reasoning as a proof for the יבום case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two cases may not be built the same way; the details come in the next part of the גמרא.
